quests.question: She packed her laptop, her charger, ___ a notebook before the conference.
quests.hint: Think about whether these three items are all going into the same bag.
quests.explanation: All three items belong on the same list of things she's bringing, so 'and' simply adds the last one.

quests.question: My neighbor waters his plants every morning ___ walks his dog right after.
quests.hint: Both actions are simply part of the same morning routine.
quests.explanation: Nothing here contrasts or depends on anything else — 'and' just links two routine actions together.

quests.question: The new phone case is thin, lightweight, ___ surprisingly durable.
quests.hint: These are three separate qualities being listed about the same case.
quests.explanation: The sentence is building a list of good qualities, and 'and' joins the final one to the rest.

quests.question: The meeting ran long, ___ everyone stayed focused until the end.
quests.hint: A long meeting usually causes people to lose focus — did that happen here?
quests.explanation: You'd expect people to tune out during a long meeting, but they didn't — that unexpected turn is a contrast.

quests.question: The jacket looked expensive, ___ it was actually on sale.
quests.hint: Its appearance pointed to one price; the real price was a different story.
quests.explanation: The jacket's expensive look clashes with its actual low price, and 'but' signals that mismatch.

quests.question: We arrived at the airport early, ___ our flight was delayed by two hours anyway.
quests.hint: Arriving early should have meant less waiting — did it work out that way?
quests.explanation: Being early made no difference in the end, and 'but' points out that ironic contrast.

quests.question: Would you like your coffee hot ___ iced?
quests.hint: The customer will end up with just one of these two.
quests.explanation: Only one option gets chosen here, and 'or' is exactly how you offer two alternatives.

quests.question: You can send the report today ___ wait until the morning meeting.
quests.hint: These are two possible paths, and the person will take one of them.
quests.explanation: Two separate options are being laid out for the reader to pick between, which is exactly what 'or' does.

quests.question: Tap the blue icon ___ swipe left to see more options.
quests.hint: These are two different ways to reach the same result — you'd only need one.
quests.explanation: The instructions describe two separate methods for the same goal, so 'or' shows they're alternatives, not steps to do together.

quests.question: The wind picked up suddenly, ___ we packed up the picnic early.
quests.hint: The wind is the cause — what did it lead the group to do?
quests.explanation: The sudden wind is the cause, and packing up is what followed from it, which is the pattern 'so' introduces.

quests.question: Rent went up again this year, ___ I started looking for a cheaper apartment.
quests.hint: The rising rent pushed the speaker toward a new decision.
quests.explanation: The rent increase is what drove the search for a cheaper place, so 'so' marks that cause-and-effect link.

quests.question: My back was hurting all week, ___ I booked an appointment with a physiotherapist.
quests.hint: The pain is what pushed the speaker to take action.
quests.explanation: Booking the appointment happened because of the back pain, and 'so' introduces that outcome.

quests.question: The workshop was postponed ___ the guest speaker came down with the flu.
quests.hint: The illness is the explanation behind the schedule change.
quests.explanation: The speaker's illness is the reason the workshop got postponed, which is exactly what 'because' introduces.

quests.question: He rewrote the whole essay ___ his laptop crashed before he could save it.
quests.hint: Something went wrong first, and that's what forced the extra work.
quests.explanation: The laptop crash is the reason all that rewriting was necessary, so 'because' fits here.

quests.question: The coach benched two players ___ they missed practice all week.
quests.hint: Their absence from practice is what led to the coach's decision.
quests.explanation: Missing practice is the reason behind the benching, and 'because' explains that link.

quests.question: The app sends a notification ___ your package leaves the warehouse.
quests.hint: The alert is tied to one exact moment in the delivery process.
quests.explanation: The notification fires at the specific moment the package leaves, and 'when' marks that exact point in time.

quests.question: Call me ___ you land at the airport.
quests.hint: The call should happen right at the moment of landing, not earlier.
quests.explanation: Landing is the trigger moment for the call, so 'when' is used to point to that exact time.

quests.question: Everyone applauded ___ the new manager announced the bonus.
quests.hint: The applause broke out at the exact instant of the announcement.
quests.explanation: The clapping starts right at the moment of the announcement, which is what 'when' signals.

quests.question: Check the departure board ___ you head to the gate.
quests.hint: One action should come earlier, so the other one is based on accurate information.
quests.explanation: Checking the board needs to happen first so the gate information is correct, and 'before' places it ahead of the other action.

quests.question: Let the pan heat up ___ you add the oil.
quests.hint: One step needs a head start, so the next step goes in properly.
quests.explanation: The pan needs time to heat first, and 'before' shows that the oil goes in only after that earlier step.

quests.question: Please review the contract carefully ___ you sign it.
quests.hint: Reading needs to happen first, so the signature comes with full understanding.
quests.explanation: The review has to come earlier than the signature, and 'before' sets up that required order.

quests.question: She stretches for ten minutes ___ every run.
quests.hint: The stretching is a cool-down, not a warm-up.
quests.explanation: The stretching happens once the run is finished, so 'after' places it in that later position.

quests.question: The store restocked its shelves ___ the holiday rush finally ended.
quests.hint: The busy period had to fully pass before the new stock could go out.
quests.explanation: The restocking only happened once the entire rush was over, which is the later-time meaning of 'after'.

quests.question: We usually watch a movie together ___ dinner is finished.
quests.hint: The movie is the second part of the evening, not the first.
quests.explanation: Dinner comes first and the movie follows, so 'after' marks the movie as the later event.

quests.question: She answered emails ___ she waited for the meeting to start.
quests.hint: Both things were happening together during the same stretch of time.
quests.explanation: Answering emails and waiting were happening at the same time, and 'while' links two ongoing actions like that.

quests.question: He hums along to the radio ___ he washes the dishes.
quests.hint: Both activities are happening at once, side by side.
quests.explanation: Humming and washing dishes overlap in time rather than one following the other, which is what 'while' expresses.

quests.question: Many commuters read on their phones ___ they ride the subway.
quests.hint: The reading fills the same time as the ride itself, not before or after it.
quests.explanation: The reading takes place during the ride, at the same time, which 'while' is built to describe.

quests.question: The design team kept revising the logo ___ the client finally approved it.
quests.hint: The revising continued right up to one final stopping point.
quests.explanation: The revisions kept going up to the moment of approval, and 'until' marks that ending point of a continuing action.

quests.question: Keep icing the sprain ___ the swelling goes down.
quests.hint: The icing should continue right up to the point when the swelling stops.
quests.explanation: Icing is meant to continue up to the point where the swelling disappears, which is the stopping point 'until' introduces.

quests.question: Keep your receipt ___ the return period ends.
quests.hint: The receipt stays useful right up to one final cutoff.
quests.explanation: The receipt needs to be kept up to the closing date of the return window, which is the endpoint meaning of 'until'.
